abstract: Employee voice -- the discretionary expression of ideas, concerns, and suggestions intended to improve organizational functioning -- creates value inside firms, yet organizations increasingly replace or augment human-led listening with AI-enabled systems that collect, analyze, and route employee input at scale. Whether algorithmic listening replicates the value-creation mechanisms of human voice, and whether it alters the pathways through which voice translates into performance, remains an open question. This research proposal theorizes that traditional voice bundles two distinct functions, knowledge extraction and relational signaling, and that AI mediation may decouple them: strengthening the informational pathway (implemented improvement measures) while weakening the affective pathway (the experience of being heard). We propose a randomized field intervention at a global strategy consulting firm, covering approximately 2,000 client-facing consultants, that varies the form of listening across three conditions -- no structured voice, human-led survey-based voice, and AI-enabled conversational voice -- and links weekly team survey data to longitudinal performance ratings. A dual-mediation model is tested in which voice affects performance through (1) implemented process improvements and (2) affective well-being. The study extends voice theory to knowledge-intensive professional services, disentangles the micro-mechanisms of voice, and provides causal evidence on whether AI can serve as an effective listener.

ob.ai_reason: AI中介的员工建言，AI核心，OB核心议题
ob.tldr: 针对组织用AI系统替代或增强人工倾听员工意见的趋势，研究者提出将员工建言拆分为信息提取（知识）与关系信号（被倾听感）双功能，并假设AI介导会强化信息路径（改进措施落地）而弱化情感路径（被倾听体验）。拟在一家全球战略咨询公司约2000名顾问中开展三组随机现场实验（无结构化建言、人工问卷建言、AI对话建言），通过双中介模型检验建言通过流程改进与情感幸福感影响绩效的机制。

title: AI-Mediated Employee Voice and Performance: Disentangling Informational and Affective Pathways
title_zh: AI中介的员工建言与绩效：厘清信息性与情感性路径
